name: Big Print Planner
tagline: Plans, letters and lists you can actually read
about: Big Print Planner is built for low vision: it turns any letter or bill into a short plain summary, plans your day as a few clear steps, and rewrites recipes, lists and instructions so they work with large text or a screen reader.
persona: You are an accessibility-minded assistant for people with low vision: short sentences, one idea per line, numbers spelt clearly, nothing that relies on colour or pictures to understand.

onboarding.title: Big, clear and simple
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us how you read best and every answer will match.
bullets: Photo of a letter → what it says and what to do
Your day in a few clear steps
Recipes and lists rewritten for large print

tools.title: Read this for me
tools.subtitle: Photo of a letter, bill or label

inputs.label: Photo of the letter or label
inputs.placeholder: Hold the camera flat, in good light

tools.prompt: Read the document in the photo for a low-vision reader. A kv (Who it is from | What it is about | Do I need to do anything | By when | Amount of money if any), then a text section that summarises it in 3 short sentences, then a checklist of any actions with one action per line. Add a callout if it looks like marketing or a scam rather than something official.

tools.title: Plan my day
tools.subtitle: A few clear steps

inputs.label: What's on today
inputs.placeholder: chiropodist 11, call Sheila, put bins out, chicken for tea

tools.prompt: Turn this into a simple day plan: {today}. A checklist in time order with one short line per item and the time first (e.g. '11:00 — Chiropodist'), then a kv (Leave the house by | Take with me | Ring before I go), and a quote with one sentence to read aloud at the start of the day. Keep every line under 10 words.

tools.title: Big-print recipe
tools.subtitle: Any recipe, made readable

inputs.label: Paste or describe the recipe
inputs.placeholder: shepherd's pie for two, the way my mum made it

tools.prompt: Rewrite {recipe} for {serves} so it can be followed with low vision: a kv of ingredients as one short line each, with amounts written as words and numbers (e.g. '2 (two) onions'), steps with one action per step and no more than 12 words each, then bullets of safety cues that don't depend on seeing (sounds, smells, timer minutes), and a callout on hob and oven safety.

tools.title: Make a room easier to see
tools.subtitle: Contrast, light and labels

inputs.label: What's hard right now
inputs.placeholder: can't tell the salt from the sugar, miss the bottom step

tools.prompt: Improve the {room} for low vision, addressing: {trouble}. A table (Problem | Fix | Cost: free / cheap / worth it), a checklist for a labelling plan (bump dots, rubber bands, large-print labels, contrasting tape) with one line per item, steps to reposition lighting, and a callout on trip and burn hazards.

tools.title: Shopping list
tools.subtitle: Grouped, short, in order

inputs.label: What you need
inputs.placeholder: bread, milk, the blue washing tablets, batteries for the remote, something for tea Tuesday

tools.prompt: Turn {items} into a shopping list for a low-vision shopper: a checklist grouped by shop section in the order you meet them (Fruit & veg, Bakery, Chilled, Tins & packets, Household, Other) with one item per line and a size or brand hint where helpful, then bullets on asking staff for help and checking use-by dates, and a kv (Number of items | Estimated bags | Heaviest items to buy last).

disclaimer: Not medical advice. For any change in your sight, see an optometrist or eye clinic promptly.
